raw_output: {"rationale":"This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or Integrator feedback yet. The design is a reasoned starting point from the contract, not an evidence-based fit. Five sensors spread across ±0.02 m cover the 25 mm tape with overlap, so the line stays visible through moderate bends and a small lateral offset. Sensors sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle so the reading leads the wheels and gives the controller time to react before the robot drifts. A 0.012 m footprint gives a graded response across the tape edge without much blur. The wheel track of 0.12 m and wheel radius of 0.03 m keep turning responsive without being twitchy. Mass 0.7 kg and body length 0.16 m keep yaw inertia low, which helps reach roughly 1.5 m/s on a 3 s clock. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), so body_width 0.10 gives 0.06 m, the same as any width up to about 0.19 m. I chose 0.10 m for a compact, low-inertia body.
